title: config.example.toml uses non-existent allow_non_loopback key
description: The example configs (crates/transit/config.example.toml line 31 and crates/reader/config.example.toml line 17) both contain a commented line '# allow_non_loopback = false' — but this field does not exist in AdminConfig for transit or reader. The transit AdminConfig has 'bearer_token'; the reader AdminConfig has 'admin_token'. An operator who uncomments this line gets a silent parse error or it is silently ignored by serde, while the field documentation in docs/ops/configuration_reference.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/debugging.md, and docs/spikes/admin_auth_options.md all describe this knob as if it were real. This means an operator who follows the docs and sets allow_non_loopback = true to expose the admin endpoint gets no error but also no actual opt-in — the non-loopback enforcement silently applies the real guard (bearer_token/admin_token check), while the operator believes they have opted in to unauthenticated access. Maintenance consequence: every docs update touching admin config must stay in sync with a field that does not exist, and any contributor who adds it will create an actual security bypass.
